question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{32}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -7 & 10 \\ -9 & -1 & -6 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & 2 & -6 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 & -7\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+{C}_{2} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-1){C}_{2} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -1 & -5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-1 & -5 & 4 \\ -10 & -5 & 6 \\ 3 & 3 & -4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
